title: Connect the Banks
subtitle: Give the script your two Plaid keys, set the history start date, connect each bank once, turn on the nightly sync, and do your first review. The code is already in your Sheet (deployed from GitHub). After the November 7 merge, run Upgrade workbook once so the new Debts columns exist.
intro: Everything here happens inside the Sheet and the Plaid dashboard; there is nothing to paste. Each bank uses one of the 20 free Plaid slots for good, so connect each institution exactly once and use **Repair** for problems.
**Privacy:** the two Plaid keys go into the script's Script Properties only — never into a cell, a chat, an email or GitHub.
Do the bank sign-ins at home or on cellular, not on public Wi-Fi.

steps.text: Reload the Sheet. The **Finance Tracker** menu should start with *Import reviewed rows* and contain a **Bank feed** submenu. Open **Import Rules** and **Connections**: both tabs exist (between Import Staging and Change Log) with blue header rows.
steps.note: If the menu still looks like the old one, the deploy has not run yet; check the Actions tab on GitHub or tell me.

steps.text: Run **Finance Tracker → Upgrade workbook (keeps data)** once. It adds the new Debts columns, the Connections column, the **Goals** and **Reminders** tabs, adds the **Paste Import** and **Expected Income** tabs, the new Monthly Plan columns, rebuilds the **Dashboard** with the accounts block at the top, puts the tabs in the new order (Dashboard, Savings & Reserves, Debts first), adds Pension to the Account Type list and the settings on App Setup. Your rows are untouched.
steps.note: Skip this if the upgrade report already lists those columns. It takes well under a minute.

steps.text: Run **Finance Tracker → Bank feed → Sync now**. Google asks you to approve one new permission (sending email, for reminders); approve it. The sync then reports each connection and may show debt rows updated from the lender.
steps.note: Until that approval is given once, the nightly sync cannot run. Everything else works without it.

steps.text: Run **Finance Tracker → Run QA checks**. Expect PASS throughout, including the new Import Staging / Import Rules / Connections lines.
steps.note: If anything says FAIL, send me the line.

sections.heading: Give the script your Plaid keys

steps.text: In a new browser tab open [dashboard.plaid.com](https://dashboard.plaid.com) and sign in. In the left sidebar choose **Developers → Keys**. You need two values: **client_id** and the **Production** secret (the free Trial runs against Production; do not use the Sandbox secret).
steps.note: Keep this tab open; you will copy from it twice.

steps.text: In the Sheet choose **Extensions → Apps Script**, then click the gear **Project Settings**. Scroll to **Script Properties** → **Add script property**. Property `PLAID_CLIENT_ID`, Value: your client_id. **Add script property** again: Property `PLAID_SECRET`, Value: the Production secret. Click **Save script properties**.
steps.note: Spelling matters: capitals and underscores exactly as shown. These two boxes are the only place the keys ever live.

steps.text: Back in the Sheet choose **Finance Tracker → Bank feed → Status**. It should say PLAID_CLIENT_ID: set, PLAID_SECRET: set, 0 of 20 connections.
steps.note: "missing" means a property name is misspelled. The status never shows the values themselves.

steps.text: Choose **Bank feed → Set history start date…** and enter the first day you want imported as yyyy-mm-dd (for example the first of this month).
steps.note: Set it before connecting the first bank: it also decides how much history Plaid is asked for. Transactions before that day are ignored.

steps.text: Choose **Bank feed → Connect a bank…**. Leave **Spending account** selected, click **Continue**, then **Open Plaid to connect your bank**. In Plaid's tab search `Independent Bank`, pick the Michigan one, sign in, select all three accounts (checking, savings, credit card). When Plaid says you are done, close that tab.
steps.note: Plaid never shows us your bank password; the sign-in happens on Plaid's and the bank's own pages.

steps.text: Back in the dialog click **I've finished in Plaid**. Step 3 lists the three accounts. Match them: Checking → ACC-007, Savings → ACC-008, Credit Card → ACC-009. Leave **Import transactions** ticked for all three. Click **Save and run the first sync**.
steps.note: If it says "not finished yet", complete Plaid's steps and click again. If an account matches no row, choose Create a new Accounts row. If you closed this dialog after Plaid said Success, nothing is lost: run Bank feed → Finish connecting and it reopens on this matching step for that bank, using no new slot.

steps.text: The dialog reports how many transactions landed in Import Staging and how many balances were updated. Open **Connections**: CONN-001 Independent Bank, Status Active. Open **Accounts**: ACC-007/008/009 show External Account ID, Connection ID and a fresh Current Balance.
steps.note: A long Last Error on Connections is something to send me.

steps.text: Repeat **Connect a bank…** as a **Spending account** for Capital One (→ ACC-010), PayPal (→ ACC-006), **American Express** (Create a new Accounts row) and **Venmo** (Create a new Accounts row). Capital One and Amex send you to their own login pages inside Plaid; that is expected. In step 3 the dialog now pre-selects your matching Accounts row when the bank and account type line up; check it before saving.
steps.note: Capital One also returns the auto loan as a second account: leave it on Create a new Accounts row with Import transactions unticked (balance only); the car payment itself is recorded from checking. If a connection fails halfway, use Bank feed → Repair a connection…, never Connect again for the same bank.

steps.text: Repeat **Connect a bank…** as **Investment or retirement account** for Acorns (→ ACC-011) and Fidelity (→ ACC-012), and as **Balance only — any account type** for HealthEquity (→ ACC-013), leaving *Ask Plaid for* on **Account details (try this first)**. Leave **Import transactions** unticked for these; they update balances only.
steps.note: Plaid will not open a connection that asks for nothing, so Balance only asks for account details, which the tracker never reads. If HealthEquity shows a red flag in Plaid's search for that too, close Plaid's tab, click Back, pick **Account-holder details** in the Ask Plaid for box and try once more. If it is flagged for both, Plaid cannot connect it: type the HSA balance into ACC-013's Current Balance on Accounts when you review it instead. Failed attempts use no slot. If Fidelity shows a request-access message, approve it and try again in a day. Bank feed → Status should end at 9 of 20.

steps.text: Repeat **Connect a bank…** as **Loan or student loan servicer** for each of your two student loan servicers (the company whose website you sign in to and pay: for example Nelnet, MOHELA, Aidvantage, EdFinancial). In step 3 choose **Whose loans are these?** (Ben or Valerie), leave every row on Create a new Accounts row, Import transactions unticked, and save.
steps.note: Every loan the servicer lists becomes a Debts row under Student Loans: your empty Student loan row for that person is used first, the rest are created. The first sync fills balance, interest rate, minimum payment, due day, repayment plan and original principal. Two slots (11 of 20 when everything is connected).

steps.text: Choose **Bank feed → Turn nightly sync on**. The feed then runs every morning around 5 AM; **Bank feed → Sync now** runs it any time.
steps.note: Approve the permission prompt if Google asks.

sections.heading: PSLF counts and credit scores (the two things with no feed)

steps.text: Sign in to studentaid.gov, open your loan details and note the **qualifying payment count** for each person's loans. On **Debts**, type it into **PSLF Official Count** on that person's loan rows and today's date into **PSLF Count As Of**.
steps.note: Plaid cannot supply this number. From here the tracker counts each month you make a payment to that loan and shows PSLF Estimated Count and PSLF Remaining (of 120); the Debts band and the Dashboard footnote show the lowest loan per person. Re-check studentaid.gov every six months or so and update the count and date: the estimate resets to the official figure.

steps.text: After the first paycheck and loan payment arrive, confirm the loan payments are recorded as **Debt Payment** with the right **Debt ID** (the rule you make from the first one does this every month). That is what the PSLF count reads.
steps.note: If a servicer takes both people's payments from the same checking account, make one rule per servicer description and set the Debt ID on it.

steps.text: Reminders take care of the rest: the **Reminders** tab (fourth tab) lists any loan whose PSLF count is missing or older than the setting on App Setup (**PSLF count reminder after (months)**, 12 to start) and any person whose latest credit score on the Credit Scores tab is missing or older than **Credit score reminder after (months)** (3 to start). While something is listed, the nightly sync emails you once a month. **Finance Tracker → Show reminders** shows the same list any time.
steps.note: Change the months on App Setup if you want it sooner (6) or later. Untick Email reminders there to stop the emails and keep the box.

sections.heading: Your weekly review, with real rows

steps.text: Open **Import Staging**. New rows have Status **Needs Review**. Fill or fix Suggested Type / Category / Subcategory / Spending Type with the dropdowns, then tick **Reviewed?** on each row you are happy with.
steps.note: Transfers between your own accounts and credit-card payments are detected and imported automatically (Status Imported, Paired Import ID filled). Turn that off on App Setup if you ever want to see them first.

steps.text: For a bill, subscription or paycheck that is always the same, click its row and choose **Finance Tracker → Make a rule from the selected row…**, check the match text, tick **Always auto-import**, save. The rule applies to every waiting row that matches and every future one.
steps.note: For a paycheck: Type Income, the person, Always auto-import. The amount is not part of the rule.

steps.text: For Meijer, Walmart, Target or Costco, make a rule with **Split required** ticked instead. Those rows then show **Needs Split**: click one and choose **Finance Tracker → Split the selected row…**, add a line per category until Remaining reads $0.00, then **Save split**.
steps.note: The receipt-photo version of this is the next phase.

steps.text: Choose **Finance Tracker → Import reviewed rows**. Ticked rows become transactions; anything missing a category is listed with the reason and stays. The Dashboard's top-right note shows how many rows are still waiting.
steps.note: Then try Finance Tracker → Copy financial snapshot for AI… and paste it into a Claude project.

steps.text: Open the new **Goals** tab (third tab, right after the Dashboard). Click into **Goal 1**'s big box and type the goal in your own words, as long as you like; the box wraps the text. Use the five boxes however suits you.
steps.note: These boxes are yours: upgrades keep the text. When you later want goals split into monthly, yearly and five-year targets, tell me and we build that on top.

sections.heading: Dashboard accounts block and typed rows

steps.text: Open the **Dashboard**. The first block shows Checking and Savings (Independent Bank) with tonight's balance and when it synced, and the three credit cards with the amount owed, the due date from the lender, and a total owed. The Selected Month and the monthly cards now sit under a "This month" bar beneath it.
steps.note: Lines read "not connected yet" until that bank is connected; Independent Bank's will fill in once its connection goes through. The Selected Month input moved to B10.

steps.text: When you type a new row on any table, for example a bill on **Recurring Payments**, the ID in column A fills in by itself as soon as you enter the name, Active is ticked, and entering a Due Day fills Next Payment Date. Totals and the Dashboard count the row from then on.
steps.note: Your rent row already has REC-001 and Active. Add its Due Day so it appears in "Due in the next 14 days".

steps.text: On your computer, download the folder `skills/paystub-import` from the repository (GitHub → Code → Download ZIP, then keep just that folder) and zip it so the zip contains `SKILL.md` and `reference/`. In claude.ai open **Settings → Capabilities → Skills**, upload the zip, and make sure skills are on in your Household Finance Tracker project.
steps.note: One-time setup. The skill holds column names and rules only, no amounts.

steps.text: In the project, upload a pay stub photo or PDF (several at once is fine, either person) and say "import these pay stubs". Claude shows a review table; correct anything wrong, then it gives you a code block that starts with HFT-IMPORT.
steps.note: Claude puts the stub's printed net pay in a check column; the Sheet compares it with gross minus deductions and notes any difference on the row.

steps.text: Copy the whole block. In the Sheet choose **Finance Tracker → Import from Claude (paste)…**, paste it into the window and click **Check it**. It lists each row it will add and anything it will skip. Click **Import N row(s)**. The Income tab gains one row per stub with an ID.
steps.note: The same block imported twice adds nothing. If you prefer, the Paste Import tab still works: paste at A5 and run Finance Tracker → Import the Paste Import tab.

sections.heading: Expected income and the automatic spending target

steps.text: After the upgrade, open the new **Expected Income** tab (right after Income). It has one row per regular paycheck, made from the stubs you imported. Check two things on each row: **Pay Frequency** (Weekly, Biweekly, Semimonthly or Monthly) and **Typical Take-Home (per paycheck)**. Fix either by typing over it.
steps.note: Rows made from a single stub guess Biweekly and say so in Notes. Untick Active on a paycheck that has ended. Expected Monthly Take-Home on the right is what the plan works from.

steps.text: Open **Monthly Plan**. For this month, Expected Take-Home (auto), Bills, Debt Payments and Planned Savings fill in and **Flexible Target (auto)** is what is left. Leave **Monthly Flexible Target** blank to use it; type a number there only to override a month. Put extra income or a shortfall for the month in **Income Adjustment**.
steps.note: Bills come from active Recurring Payments (rent is there; the rest build up as you make rules from bills in review). Planned Savings is the Planned Monthly column on Savings & Reserves: raise it to send more to savings and the flexible target drops to match.

steps.text: Back on the **Dashboard**, the line under the four month cards reads "Expected this month: take-home … − bills … − debt payments … − planned savings … = flexible …". Current Flexible Spending further down shows the weekly guidance from that figure and says whether the target is automatic or set by hand.
steps.note: The actual cards above the line still show what has landed so far this month, so you can see both.
